sources.title: Decoupling of wages from productivity: Macro-level facts
sources.logical_locator: Abstract; OECD Economics Department Working Papers No. 1373
sources.revision_notes: Retrospective cross-country analysis; not a historical release-vintage panel.
sources.source_fact_summary: Across most OECD countries studied, productivity growth decoupled from real median compensation growth; declining labour shares and the median-to-average wage ratio contributed.

sources.title: The Fall of the Labor Share and the Rise of Superstar Firms
sources.logical_locator: Abstract; U.S. Economic Census evidence since 1982
sources.revision_notes: Working paper later published in QJE 2020; retrospective mechanism evidence.
sources.source_fact_summary: Industries became more concentrated in high-profit, lower-labor-share superstar firms; industries with larger concentration increases had larger labor-share declines.

sources.title: Short-term economic statistics revisions
sources.logical_locator: Dataset description: monthly snapshots of originally published short-term statistics
sources.revision_notes: Historical publication snapshots exist; exact country/series T0 coverage remains a G2 audit.
sources.source_fact_summary: OECD provides monthly snapshots of originally published short-term statistics for simulated real-time and revisions analysis.

sources.title: FRED API Real-Time Periods
sources.issuer: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
sources.logical_locator: Introduction: real-time periods; FRED versus ALFRED
sources.revision_notes: Method capability; actual YKS0 series still require per-series vintage audit.
sources.source_fact_summary: ALFRED real-time periods identify when information was known and allow retrieval of information known as of historical periods, including revised observations.

sources.title: Distributional Financial Accounts: corporate equities and mutual fund shares
sources.issuer: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.logical_locator: Series WFRBSB50203; Q1 2026; DFA notes
sources.revision_notes: Current distributional snapshot; historical vintages require separate audit.
sources.source_fact_summary: In Q1 2026 the bottom 50% held 1.1% of aggregate corporate equities and mutual fund shares under the Federal Reserve DFA measure.

sources.title: S&P 500 Equal Weight Index
sources.logical_locator: Overview; Quick Facts; Performance Disclosure
sources.revision_notes: Index launched 2003-01-08; all pre-launch history is hypothetical back-tested and not PIT-native.
sources.source_fact_summary: The equal-weight index launched on 8 January 2003; S&P states all prior history is hypothetical back-tested rather than live index performance.

sources.title: U.S. equity concentration in the shadows of giants
sources.issuer: S&P Global / S&P Dow Jones Indices
sources.logical_locator: Top-10 S&P 500 weight discussion around mid-2025
sources.revision_notes: Current/retrospective market concentration evidence.
sources.source_fact_summary: The largest ten S&P 500 companies represented roughly 40% of the index around mid-2025, an unusually high concentration by long-run standards.

sources.title: Germany bargaining decentralisation and productivity-to-wage pass-through
sources.logical_locator: p.26: collective bargaining coverage and productivity-to-wage pass-through
sources.revision_notes: Retrospective institutional analysis.
sources.source_fact_summary: Germany's collective bargaining coverage fell from about 85% in 1990 to below 60% in 2015; OECD notes possible implications for productivity-to-wage pass-through.

sources.title: DAX factsheet and benchmark comparison
sources.logical_locator: Performance and annual returns; DAX versus Regulated Market All Share
sources.revision_notes: Relative market evidence; sector/global exposure is a confounder and domestic K causality is not established.
sources.source_fact_summary: The displayed DAX recent annual-return figures exceed those for the Regulated Market All Share, but the index and broad market have materially different composition.

sources.title: Why did productivity gains not translate into wage gains? Lessons from Japan's deflationary period
sources.logical_locator: Abstract / Research LAB No.26-J-2
sources.revision_notes: Retrospective BOJ research; not a historical vintage source.
sources.source_fact_summary: Since the late 1990s Japan's productivity rose while real wages were broadly flat; the BOJ study links the widening gap partly to nominal wage rigidity and preference for employment stability.

sources.title: Economic Activity, Prices, and Monetary Policy in Japan — Fukuoka speech
sources.logical_locator: Chart 10 discussion: operating profit per employee at small versus large firms
sources.revision_notes: Uses Ministry of Finance corporate statistics retrospectively.
sources.source_fact_summary: Operating profit per employee at small firms was 40% of large firms in Apr-Dec 1990 and 13% in Apr-Dec 2024.

sources.title: TOPIX Large70 factsheet, 31 October 2025
sources.logical_locator: Index Performance (Total Return): 1Y and 3Y
sources.revision_notes: D-A counterexample; not a historical replay proof.
sources.source_fact_summary: As of 31 Oct 2025, TOPIX Large70 returned 21.20% over one year versus 26.70% for TOPIX; its three-year cumulative return was also lower.

sources.title: Reforming the large business groups to promote productivity and inclusion in Korea
sources.logical_locator: Opening section on large groups, exports and employment
sources.revision_notes: Retrospective structural analysis.
sources.source_fact_summary: The top 30 Korean business groups accounted for only 2.7% of employment in 2017; OECD reports weakened trickle-down as groups became more internationalised and capital/technology intensive.

sources.title: OECD Reviews of Innovation Policy: Korea 2023
sources.logical_locator: SME productivity and employment discussion
sources.revision_notes: Current/retrospective structural evidence.
sources.source_fact_summary: More than 83% of Korean workers are employed by SMEs while SME labour productivity is far below that of large firms, illustrating a large firm-size productivity gap.

sources.title: OECD Compendium of Productivity Indicators 2026 — labour productivity patterns across firm sizes
sources.logical_locator: Economy-wide patterns: Korea 2013-2024 SME catch-up
sources.revision_notes: Strong rediffusion/catch-up counter-signal; nominal turnover per employed person metric.
sources.source_fact_summary: Between 2013 and 2024 Korean SME productivity grew 3.7% annually versus 0.8% for large firms, the most pronounced SME catch-up in the OECD comparison.

sources.title: STOXX South Korea 200 factsheet
sources.logical_locator: Risk and return figures; 2025 annual returns; comparison with South Korea Total Market
sources.revision_notes: Relative large-cohort versus broad-market evidence only; does not prove K causality.
sources.source_fact_summary: The South Korea 200 returned 70.5% in 2025 versus 64.8% for the South Korea Total Market; as of July 2026 its YTD and one-year returns also exceeded the broad benchmark.

sources.title: 2025 National Economic and Social Development Statistical Communique
sources.issuer: National Bureau of Statistics of China
sources.logical_locator: Section I 综合: GDP, per-capita GDP, labour productivity
sources.revision_notes: Official current release; not yet reconstructed for historical T0 case use.
sources.source_fact_summary: In 2025 GDP grew 5.0%, per-capita GDP 5.1%, and labour productivity 6.1%.

sources.title: 2025 household income and consumption expenditure
sources.issuer: National Bureau of Statistics of China
sources.logical_locator: Table 1: disposable income median and consumption expenditure
sources.revision_notes: Official current release.
sources.source_fact_summary: In 2025 national median disposable income grew 4.4%, urban median income 3.7%, and real per-capita consumption expenditure 4.4%, slower than labour productivity growth.

sources.title: Profit of Industrial Enterprises above the Designated Size in 2025
sources.issuer: National Bureau of Statistics of China
sources.logical_locator: Industry profit table; electronics manufacturing
sources.revision_notes: Industry dispersion, not firm-level concentration.
sources.source_fact_summary: In 2025 computer/communications/electronics manufacturing profit rose 19.5% while several traditional industries contracted, showing large cross-industry profit dispersion.

sources.title: Industrial profits, January-May 2026
sources.issuer: National Bureau of Statistics of China
sources.logical_locator: Industry table: electronics, autos, non-metallic minerals
sources.revision_notes: Current cross-industry snapshot; not a historical replay source.
sources.source_fact_summary: Jan-May 2026 electronics manufacturing profit rose 103.9%, while auto manufacturing fell 19.8% and non-metallic mineral products fell 48.9%.

sources.title: World Development Indicators — Gini index, China
sources.logical_locator: WDI series SI.POV.GINI; China 2020-2022
sources.revision_notes: WDI retrospective series; release-vintage history not established here.
sources.source_fact_summary: China's WDI Gini values were 37.1 in 2020, 35.7 in 2021 and 36.0 in 2022, so the recent series does not show a simple monotonic rise.
